subject: Late burst consumption adjudication and upgrade path
messages:
From: Alice Huang <alice.huang@greengrid.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: ops@greengrid.com
Date: 2027-08-25T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected July burst — reconciliation request

Markus,

We noticed a sustained burst of inference hours from our production cluster between 2027-07-08 and 2027-07-22 that pushed us ~82% over the committed capacity in our July invoice. The attached CSV has hourly usage from our side and there are a couple of batches we still can't map to our jobs.

Can Redwood help reconcile (a) the raw request ids for the largest spikes, and (b) propose an equitable settlement? We are evaluating two paths: a one-time make-good charge and a scaled-up committed tier for the remainder of the year.

We'd like to finalize something before our next finance cycle (first week of Sept).

Thanks,
Alice Huang
Director, Platform Engineering — GreenGrid

Attachments: usage_report_Jun-Jul.csv
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Huang <alice.huang@greengrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected July burst — reconciliation request

Hi Alice — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. I pulled the Redwood side logs and attached an annotated invoice that highlights the top 12 spike windows and the corresponding request ids. A few quick notes:

- The largest cluster of overage originates from a bot-driven batch job that retried several long-running requests (we have the request ids annotated).
- A couple of mid-sized windows look like legitimate traffic increases tied to a product rollout you mentioned in June.
- We can offer two settlement options:
  1) One-off charge for the incremental usage (we propose $18,450) and a pro-rated top-up to your existing committed tier for Aug–Dec to smooth monthly variability.
  2) Immediate upgrade to the next reserved capacity tier (3x commit) with a 20% onboarding credit applied against the July overage and the first month of the new tier.

I'm copying Ben (commercial) and Laura (finance) to weigh-in on pricing mechanics and invoicing. Grace — FYI in case we need to schedule a short exec alignment with GreenGrid.

I attached the annotated invoice (annotated_invoice_v2.pdf) with notes. Let me know which path you prefer and we can produce a clear statement of work and revised invoice.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: annotated_invoice_v2.pdf

On 2027-08-25 Alice Huang <alice.huang@greengrid.com> wrote:
> Markus,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-08-26T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected July burst — reconciliation request

Markus / Laura — quick internal take before we respond to Alice:

- Option 1 (one-off $18,450): clean, straightforward; we issue an invoice for the overage and offer a 5% service credit if GreenGrid signs a 12-month commit amendment within 14 days.
- Option 2 (upgrade + 20% onboarding credit): attractive for GreenGrid but impacts revenue recognition; finance needs to apply the onboarding credit against the July overage as a credit memo, not a straight discount. Laura, can you confirm we can run credit memo GG-CR-402 and have accounting apply it to invoice INV-202707-GG?

Also: recommend we add a clause to the amendment that caps future burst overages at 1.5x committed monthly baseline for 60 days after the upgrade while they complete rollout. It protects both sides and gives them breathing room.

If finance signs off, we can present both options to Alice with clear math and the draft amendment ready.

- Ben

On 2027-08-25 Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Hi Alice — thanks for the heads up...
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Huang <alice.huang@greengrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected July burst — reconciliation request

Alice — following our internal review, here are two concrete proposals and the steps to finalize. We aimed for simplicity and a path that minimizes interruption to your rollout.

Proposal A — One-time settlement (faster close)
- One-off invoice: $16,750 (we reduced our initial estimate after narrowing anomalous retries).
- Payment terms: Net 30.
- Optional: sign a 12-month amendment to maintain current tier; if signed within 14 days, Redwood will apply a 5% credit to the one-off.

Proposal B — Upgrade + credit (recommended if you expect sustained higher traffic)
- Immediate move to the next reserved tier (3x current commit) effective 2027-09-01.
- Redwood onboarding credit: 20% applied as a credit memo against INV-202707-GG (annotated_invoice_v2.pdf).
- Pro-rated charge for Sept on the new tier; we will absorb porting costs for the first week.
- Temporary burst cap: for the first 60 days after upgrade, overage billing will be capped at 1.5x your new committed baseline to reduce bill volatility.

Next steps if you choose B: sign the amendment (I attached a one-pager template link) and confirm the effective date. Laura will issue the credit memo and coordinate with billing for invoice reissue.

If you choose A: Laura will issue INV-202708-MK-01 and we’ll follow up for payment.

Please let us know which option you prefer and we’ll fast-track the paperwork. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if that helps.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: annotated_invoice_v2.pdf, usage_report_Jun-Jul.csv
